paragraphs: Khachapuri is not one bread but a Georgian family of cheese-filled breads, with forms tied to different regions. Adjarian khachapuri comes from Adjara on Georgia's Black Sea coast. paragraphs: Ackee and saltfish carries several parts of Jamaican history in one pan. Ackee came from West Africa; its Jamaican name traces to the Twi word ankye. The fruit became so closely identified with the island that it is now Jamaica's national fruit, while ackee cooked with salted cod is widely recognized as the national dish.

The pairing also reflects colonial trade and plantation life. Salted fish was durable imported food, while African cooks and their descendants shaped ingredients and techniques into a distinctly Jamaican cuisine. This version treats both ingredients with care: soak and gently flake the cod, use commercially canned ackee that has already been safely processed, and fold the tender fruit only a few times so it stays intact among the peppers, thyme, tomato, scallion, and Scotch bonnet.
